title: A JSON Schema inclusion benchmark case
description: Two schemas and what is known about them: does a accept every instance valid under b? The labels hold for draft 2020-12 with format asserted and patterns read as ECMA-262 regular expressions with the u flag.

$schema.description: The path from this file to case.schema.json, which is at the root of the corpus: above the folder of the collection and the folder of its origin.

a_subsumes_b.description: Whether a accepts every instance valid under b; null when the corpus claims nothing.

b_subsumes_a.description: The same question in the other direction.

features.description: What the two schemas use, in the order of the list of features: every keyword that validation can reach and that decides what a schema accepts, and 'recursion' when a schema is reached again from itself through a reference.

upstream.description: A permanent link to the file this case comes from, in the source repository at the commit that collections.json names for the collection; the test suite's cases add a JSON pointer to the test case or the test after a '#'.

duplicates.description: Permanent links to the other upstream files that hold these two schemas, in either order, each written like upstream. The corpus has one case for all of them, and its labels are what any of them says; absent when there is no other.

note.description: Why the labels depart from upstream's; absent when they do not.

derived.description: What shows each label that upstream does not give and that was derived from the answers of checkers; absent when the case has no such label.

a.description: The schema that should accept everything.

b.description: The schema whose instances must be accepted.

Schema.description: A schema that is valid draft 2020-12 and stands on its own: every document it references is embedded in it.

Derived.description: What shows the labels of a case that upstream does not give, by label.

Evidence.description: What shows one label: a counterexample for false, an agreement of checkers for true.

Counterexample.description: The label is false, and an instance proves it.

counterexample.description: An instance that is valid under the schema whose instances must be accepted and not valid under the schema that should accept everything.

Agreement.description: The label is true as far as checkers can tell: at least two of them say so and none that was asked says otherwise. This is evidence and no proof.

checkers.description: The checkers that say so, each with its version, sorted.

Feature.description: A keyword of draft 2020-12 that decides what a schema accepts, or 'recursion'.
